subject: Re: Request — DPA artifacts, DPIA support, and transfer assurances
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@orchard-analytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Orchard Analytics Legal <privacy@orchard-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA artifacts, DPIA and transfer assurances

Markus —

We're in the middle of completing Orchard's vendor privacy review ahead of a public-sector procurement and need to confirm a few items from Redwood so we can close the risk assessment: 

1) Signed DPA (latest version) and confirmation that Article 28/30 obligations are documented for subprocessors.
2) Current subprocessor inventory (CSV preferred) with country of processing and transfer mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, etc.).
3) Any Transfer Impact Assessment / data flow summary specific to EU-->US transfers; notes on UK addendum coverage if applicable.
4) Confirmation of audit rights (remote evidence vs onsite) and typical lead time for an auditor request. We may need a limited-scope evidence pull for logs and retention settings.
5) DPIA support: can Redwood provide a mapping or summary we can include in our DPIA (categories of personal data processed, purposes, retention, and technical controls).

Would appreciate this by COB next Tuesday (24 Mar) if possible. If you prefer to hop on a short call to walk through, happy to schedule.

Thanks,
Maria 
Maria Garcia
Head of Procurement & Privacy
Orchard Analytics

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@orchard-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA artifacts, DPIA and transfer assurances

Maria —

Thanks for the clear list. We're happy to support Orchard's review. Quick notes and plan: 

- I'll assemble the signed DPA and the executed UK addendum (if applicable) and share PDFs.
- Laura will export the current subprocessor inventory (CSV) with processing locations and the transfer mechanism column (SCC v2 / adequacy / in-country).
- Neha will prepare a short Transfer Impact Assessment summary and the high-level DPIA mapping you asked for (data categories, purposes, retention windows, encryption & pseudonymization controls).
- On audit rights: our standard contract provides remote evidence and periodic audit windows; onsite vendor audits are evaluated case-by-case and typically require 6-8 weeks lead time plus a narrow scope. We'll include the exact clause and approach.

Can we commit to providing the initial package (DPA + subprocessor CSV + TIA summary + DPIA mapping) by Tue 24 Mar EOD PST? If that timeline works I'll circulate a secure Drive link and a DocuSign copy of the signed DPA.

If you prefer a call, propose Thu 19 Mar 10:00-10:30 PST and we'll invite our security lead.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@orchard-analytics.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA artifacts, DPIA and transfer assurances

Maria —

Attached are the items we discussed:

- Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_20260324.csv (CSV) — columns: vendor_name, service_description, country, transfer_mechanism, processing_purpose, first_onboarded
- Attachment: redwood-dpa-signed-2025-12.pdf (PDF) — executed DPA (standard Redwood template signed Dec 2025).
- Attachment: transfer-impact-assessment-summary-20260324.pdf (PDF) — brief TIA covering EU/UK->US routing and mitigations (SCC v2, encryption in transit & at rest, region-specific key controls).

A few clarifications pulled from the inventory: 
- Most subprocessors operate within the EEA or US; where US-based subprocessors are used we rely on SCC v2 + our contractual assurances.
- For telemetry and logs we keep a 90-day default retention; audit log exports for contractual requests can be prepared as part of a scoped evidence request.
- Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation reports; those can be shared under NDA for the procurement process.

Next steps: if Orchard needs a more detailed DPIA artifact (e.g., a mapping with DPIA risk ratings), Neha can expand the summary into a template you can drop into your DPIA. Also confirming that onsite audits require a separate SOW and advance notice; remote evidence reviews are the typical path.

Drive link (read-only): https://drive.redwoodinference.com/s/oa-privacy-20260324
DocuSign envelope: DocuSign:0b3f-ORCH-DSIGN-2026

Best,
Laura 
Laura Bennett
Senior Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@orchard-analytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Orchard Analytics Legal <privacy@orchard-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 14:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA artifacts, DPIA and transfer assurances

Laura / Markus —

Received everything — thank you, the CSV and the TIA summary are really helpful. A couple of follow-ups: 

1) Can you confirm whether any subprocessors process special category data (sensitive personal data) on behalf of Redwood customers? We didn't see any flags in the CSV but want explicit confirmation for our DPIA.
2) For SOC 2 / ISO reports, we'll sign the mutual NDA and request those documents; can you share NDA routing instructions?
3) We may request a limited-scope log pull (authentication and access logs) for a security validation; please let us know the steps to submit a formal remote evidence request and expected SLAs.

We can take the rest of the items offline with Neha — happy to book the call if she has bandwidth next week.

Thanks again — aiming to finalize this block for our procurement on 08 Apr.

Best,
Maria
